title: Lakshmi and the Lights
audience: Families and festival audiences; a one-minute Diwali explainer about why Lakshmi is welcomed with light.
notes: The user asked for a one-minute Diwali film explaining why Lakshmi is prayed to. The facts are framed as one beloved story and qualified where traditions differ: Lakshmi is the goddess of prosperity and abundance; the Samudra Manthana is narrated in the Vishnu Purana and Bhagavata Purana; Lakshmi emerged from the churning and chose Vishnu; Lakshmi Puja is held on the new-moon night in most of India; homes are cleaned, rangoli drawn, windows opened and diyas lit; in Bengal the same night is Kali Puja, in the north it marks Rama's return, and in the west businesses open new account books. Sources: Britannica (Lakshmi, Samudra Manthana, Lakshmi Puja, Diwali), BBC Religions (Lakshmi), Sahapedia (Diwali origins), Yale Hindu Life (Lakshmi and dana). The characters are film-local paper-puppet characters (Lakshmi, Vishnu, Householder, Child), built to the Paper K-pop construction; they are not a new style identity. No fireworks are shown: the film is about lamps, not smoke.
